admin.title: Discovery rules
admin.subtitle: Map neutral signals to your device types. Loaded empty — add rules to classify hosts.
admin.help: A rule says: when a host shows this signal, propose this device type. Then open a point → Discover → Rescan, and add the matched hosts as devices.
admin.tipStrong: Tip: a bare common port (22 SSH, 80 HTTP) is open on almost every host — a port-only rule over-matches. Prefer a banner regex on the product string (e.g. "MikroTik RouterOS", "OpenSSH.*Ubuntu"), or narrow by IP range.
admin.matching: A device type is the COMBINATION of its signals: the more of a type's signals a host matches, the higher its coverage %. Highest coverage wins; on a tie, the type with more/stronger matched signals wins.
admin.patternHint: CIDR / port number / regex (depends on signal). ip_range also takes a regex starting with ^, tested against the host IP
admin.weightHint: How strong this signal is on its own (1–100). The engine sums the weights of a type's matched signals — you don't split 100% between rules.
admin.preview: This type would match {wins} of {hosts} scanned hosts ({full} full, {partial} partial).
admin.previewNone: No scans yet to test against — run Discover on a point first.
admin.empty: No rules yet — every host is classified as unknown.

admin.title: Scheduled tasks
admin.subtitle: Scripts with their own runtime, dependencies and schedule. No device needed.
admin.emptyHint: A task is a script plus its environment: pick a runtime, paste the code, add dependencies if it needs any, then give it a schedule or a webhook.
admin.noRuntimes: No task runner is configured. Set NUXT_TASK_RUNNERS in the app environment to a JSON map of runtime name to runner URL (the path must be /run-task, not /run), then restart the app.
admin.name: Name
admin.entrypointHint: Which file to run. Must be one of the files below.
admin.depsHint: Contents of requirements.txt (Python) or package.json (Node). Installed once into a cached environment, reused by later runs.
admin.depsLockHint: Pin exact versions. Part of the environment key, so changing it builds a new environment.
admin.envHint: Non-secret values only — these are stored as plain text. Secrets go through credential sets below.
admin.credRefsHint: A credential set is injected as PREFIX_USER, PREFIX_PASSWORD and PREFIX_PORT. Values are masked in the output.
admin.timeoutHint: Applies to the run itself; installing dependencies has its own limit.
admin.sinkHint: We POST a JSON summary of the run here: status, exit code, the tail of stderr, a link to the run, and whatever your task wrote into RUN_DATA_FILE. Append your own data to the URL query (a chat id, for example) and the receiving task reads it from RUN_QUERY — so one shared notifier can serve every task. Leave empty for no notifications.
admin.outputHint: Write files to the folder in RUN_OUTPUT and they show up as downloadable artifacts. The incoming webhook body is in the file named by RUN_PAYLOAD_FILE, URL query params arrive as RUN_QUERY, and anything your task writes as JSON into RUN_DATA_FILE is passed on to the receiver of the notification.
admin.createdAddTrigger: Task saved. Add a schedule or a webhook below — or just close this.
admin.deleteConfirm: Delete task "{name}"? Its run history stays in the journal.
admin.runQueued: Started — run {id} is in the journal.
admin.triggersHint: A task can have several: a schedule and a webhook at the same time.
admin.cronHint: Five fields: minute hour day month weekday. Examples: every 5 minutes is */5 * * * *, every night at 03:30 is 30 3 * * *. Shortcuts {'@'}hourly and {'@'}daily also work.
admin.syncHint: The caller waits for the task to finish and gets its output. Off means an immediate 202 with a run id.
admin.tokenOnce: Copy this URL now — the token is shown once and only its hash is stored.
admin.hookPostOnly: Send a POST with a JSON body. Opening this URL in a browser is a GET and will not run the task. Add query params (?key=value) to pass your own data — the task reads them from RUN_QUERY.
admin.builtinHint: built into the app — no script to write

builtinAbout.backup: Dumps the whole database (public, auth, storage) into BACKUP_DIR and keeps the newest BACKUP_KEEP files (7 by default). Both come from the deployment env — nothing to type here. The dump is NOT encrypted, and it is only 1 of the 3 parts of a backup set: keep NUXT_CRED_ENCRYPTION_KEY and JWT_SECRET separately.
